# Laws

<!-- Generated by scripts/laws-doc.ts from laws/*.ts; edit those, then run `bun run laws:doc`. -->

jev-fabric's policy is split the way 0.8.1's Bend was: **pure modules**
(`src/*/core.ts`, `*-core.ts` and the codec) decide, and **drivers** do the
IO (files, processes, clocks, sockets, `bun:ffi` in `src/sys/`). A pure
module imports nothing that does IO, so its rules can be stated and proven
apart from the system.

Each rule below is written as a [gdp-wired](https://github.com/monotykamary/gdp-wired)
rule and proven three ways by `bun run laws`:

- **laws**: proven by gdp-wired's kernel with no proof written by hand
  (`proveSteps` for a rule's every step, from its start or, where marked,
  from any state its laws allow; `proveDecision` for a single function);
- **bugs refused**: a broken variant of the same rule, the bug the laws are
  there to rule out, must fail the same laws;
- **held to the real code**: the rule runs beside the TypeScript that ships
  (`src/`), on random or every input, and must agree step for step.

`bun run laws` prints one row per item below and ends with `ALL LAWS PROVEN`
only when every row holds. CI runs it on every push.

## What this does not prove

This is scoped proof of the pure core, not whole-program verification. The
laws say what the policy decides; a rule held to the code is a test of
agreement on the inputs tried, not a proof that the two are equal. Outside
the laws, and covered by unit and conformance tests instead:

- the drivers: process groups, signals, deadlines that kill a group, file
  locks and leases, spools on disk, the store, `serve`'s concurrency;
- that a clock advances, that a system call returns, or that a receipt
  describes what really happened to a process;
- Bun, its `fetch` and TLS, libc, the OS, the filesystem and the CA store,
  which remain trusted;
- Jev's judgment and whether a task is really done;
- programs run with `jev-fabric -- run`: they are trusted code, not a
  sandbox, and nothing here is claimed for them.

A deadline budget is not an isolated resource group, and timing (scheduler
or launch latency) is not a hard real-time guarantee.

303 rows over 18 areas: 176 laws, 71 bugs refused, 56 comparisons with the real code.

## strict UTF-8

Rule `utf-8` (`proveSteps`, from any state):

- a sequence has at most three bytes left
- every scalar decoded is a Unicode scalar: at most U+10FFFF, never a surrogate
- no overlong form: a multi-byte scalar is at least the smallest of its length
- a stray continuation byte fails
- after a failure nothing more is decoded

Bugs refused (on the broken `utf-8`):

- surrogates decoded
- no minimum per sequence length (overlong forms)
- a stray continuation byte taken as a character

Held to the real code (`utf-8`):

- Codec.decodeUtf8 on every prefix of random bytes

## the textual scan

Rule `scan` (`proveSteps`):

- depth and work never pass their limits unless the scan failed
- inside a string nothing counts toward depth or work
- an escaped character never ends a string
- a close at depth 0 fails (no saturating underflow)

Bugs refused (on the broken `scan`):

- work counted inside strings
- an escaped quote ends the string
- a saturating close at depth 0

Held to the real code (`scan`):

- Codec.scanStep and Codec.scanText
- Codec.scanText at depth 64 and work 32768

## the number grammar

Rule `number` (`proveSteps`):

- a number ends only in a state that can end it: never after a sign, a dot or an e
- a leading zero is never followed by a digit

Bugs refused (on the broken `number`):

- a number ended after its dot
- a leading zero followed by digits

Held to the real code (`number`):

- json.parse on random lexemes

## the encoder

Rule `encoder fuel` (`proveSteps`):

- encoding_without_fuel_fails: no job runs past the fuel
- a job with no fuel left fails the encoding

Bugs refused (on the broken `encoder fuel`):

- an encoder that runs without fuel

Held to the real code (`encoder fuel`):

- json.writeWithFuel (its job count, exactly)

## exact probability mass

Rule `probability mass` (`proveSteps`):

- a distribution is taken only with its mass within [0.98, 1.02]
- no probability above 1 is taken

Bugs refused (on the broken `probability mass`):

- a tolerance of 1.03

Held to the real code (`probability mass`):

- Wire.response (exact decimals)

## the decision budget

Rule `decision budget` (`proveSteps`, from any state):

- reported tokens never pass the limit but by the one saturating step
- calls left and calls spent never pass the calls given
- a reservation needs a call and tokens left
- unknown or invalid usage stops the budget
- reported_overshoot_disables_calls: an overshoot disables every later call
- accounting_never_refunds_a_call: accounting never gives a call back
- reported tokens never go down

Bugs refused (on the broken `decision budget`):

- unknown usage that keeps the calls
- an overshoot checked only per report, not against what is left
- accounting that refunds a call

Held to the real code (`decision budget`):

- Core.reserve and Decision.account (rule.compare)

## the Jev client

Rule `jev client` (`proveSteps`):

- one budget: requests sent never pass the calls given
- a request sent is an evaluation counted: no retries
- calls left and calls spent never pass the calls given
- reservation before dispatch: a request goes out only with a call and tokens left
- validation before credentials: an invalid request runs no command and sends nothing
- a budget spent never resolves a credential
- a cached credential is never fetched again
- a deadline passed before dispatch sends nothing and spends nothing
- a failed dispatch spends its call: nothing refunds one
- a reply that fails validation is never accepted
- an overshoot disables every later call
- reported tokens never go down

Bugs refused (on the broken `jev client`):

- a failed dispatch refunded
- a failed dispatch retried
- a reservation that ignores the reported tokens
- the credential resolved before the reservation
- a dispatch after the deadline
- a cached key fetched again
- a reply that fails validation accepted

Held to the real code (`jev client`):

- JevCore.evaluation, the walk Jev.evaluate drives (answered from a script)
- JevCore.evaluation validates before any effect

## jobs

Rule `event ring` (`proveSteps`, from any state):

- at most 64 events are retained
- only events made are retained
- a sequence number is never reused: the next one only grows

Bugs refused (on the broken `event ring`):

- a ring that keeps every event

Held to the real code (`event ring`):

- Core.event (the real ring, 150 events a run)

Rule `save cadence` (`proveSteps`, from any state):

- the ticks since the last save are counted up to one interval
- a timed rest is one tick (25 ms) at least and 100 ms at most
- a change waiting to be saved rests only one tick, so it is on disk within 75 ms
- only a quiet job rests until rung
- a pending change one interval old is saved on the next tick that does not finish
- saves come at most once an interval
- a change is never forgotten unsaved
- a tick that saw output rests one tick: output keeps the 25 ms cadence
- a worker that polls its stop marker and owner never rests until rung: a stop is seen within 100 ms

Bugs refused (on the broken `save cadence`):

- a cadence that waits past its interval
- a worker that rests longer while a change waits to be saved
- a worker process that rests until rung, though nothing rings it for a stop

Held to the real code (`save cadence`):

- Core.saveDue, Core.afterTick and Core.restFor (rule.compare)
- Core.saveDue, Core.afterTick and Core.restFor over 40-tick runs, polled and announced

Rule `follow cursor` (`proveSteps`, from any state):

- the cursor never goes back past where it started
- followed_event_is_never_repeated: nothing at or before the cursor prints
- the cursor never goes back
- a gap is disclosed before the event past it

Bugs refused (on the broken `follow cursor`):

Held to the real code (`follow cursor`):

- receipt_finishes_follow: even at its ceiling (`follow end`, `proveDecision`)

Bugs refused (on the broken `follow end`):

- at most 1024 lines a stream are emitted

- every batch and pending line came from lines emitted

Rule `watch frame` (`proveSteps`, from any state):

- a partial line never passes 4096 characters
- nor does a completed one

Rule `watch cursor` (`proveSteps`, from any state):

- the cursor never goes back
- a replay at or before the cursor changes nothing
- a sequence gap counts one loss before the event past it

Bugs refused (on the broken `watch cursor`):

Held to the real code (`watch cursor`):

## serve

Rule `serve hub` (`proveSteps`):

- no request is answered twice: answers and open requests add up to the requests accepted
- a connection runs at most 16 session children
- a session child queues at most 64 writes, closes and stops
- the session concludes only once it is ending
- every accepted request is answered before the session exits
- a child's group is listed until it is reaped, and reaped at most once
- a child leaves supervision only once its group is reaped
- no session child is still supervised once the session has concluded
- no child survives the conclusion: every group started was reaped exactly once, none is left for the watchdog
- nothing is accepted once the session is ending
- an answer is written only for an open request
- the first ending wins: an ending is never undone

Bugs refused (on the broken `serve hub`):

- a hub that writes an answer with no open request
- a hub that spawns a 17th child
- a hub that queues a 65th write
- a hub that exits with a request in flight
- a hub that accepts lines after its ending
- a hub that reaps a group twice
- a hub that lets a child go with its group unreaped (and concludes over it)

Held to the real code (`serve hub`):

- src/serve/hub.ts (accept, answer, starting, spawned, reaped, finished, exited, queue, fed, end, conclude) over 120-event runs, some pressing on the bounds

Rule `serve jev client` (`proveSteps`):

- one evaluation holds the session client at a time
- no evaluation waits while the client is free
- every evaluation that arrived runs once, in turn
- a request arriving while the client is held waits its turn

Bugs refused (on the broken `serve jev client`):

- a session that lets a second evaluation take the client

Held to the real code (`serve jev client`):

- the real JevSession (each evaluation handed the client the last returned)

- a string or number id is echoed verbatim (`id echo`, `proveDecision`)
- any other id, or none, is answered as null (`id echo`, `proveDecision`)
- an id of more than 128 characters is refused (`id echo`, `proveDecision`)
- an id of at most 128 characters is never refused for its id (`id echo`, `proveDecision`)

Bugs refused (on the broken `id echo`):

- a 129-character id accepted

Held to the real code (`id echo`):

- Core.id and Core.request on every id kind and length 0..140 (every case)

- a command with no argv is refused (`argv bounds`, `proveDecision`)
- more than 57 entries are refused (64 per child, less the CLI prefix) (`argv bounds`, `proveDecision`)
- an empty command name is refused (`argv bounds`, `proveDecision`)

Bugs refused (on the broken `argv bounds`):

Held to the real code (`argv bounds`):

- a child step and its receipt grace fit in what the session has left (`deadline cut`, `proveDecision`)
- a request is never cut while the session has time for it (`deadline cut`, `proveDecision`)
- with no time left past the grace, no child is started (`deadline cut`, `proveDecision`)

Bugs refused (on the broken `deadline cut`):

Held to the real code (`deadline cut`):

- status, events, stop, list and a start handshake wait at most 15 s (`control step`, `proveDecision`)

Bugs refused (on the broken `control step`):

Held to the real code (`control step`):

- a session child never outlives its connection less the receipt grace (`session child lifetime`, `proveDecision`)

Bugs refused (on the broken `session child lifetime`):
